context.description: Every old engine test is ported, re-baselined or retired with its reason (owner ruling 2)

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM4.spec.ts (4 tests, my own run: 4 pass, 0 fail, 594 expect calls, 10 s; engine-xstate.test.ts itself: 46 pass). Given/When (header list read): the test parses the comment header of engine-xstate.test.ts into entries id, old title, class, reason. Then (every old test once): I confirmed from git that the old file (b517ebb3f3^, also 3e57ac078c^ before the goal touched it) holds exactly the 29 titles the test pins (27 XStateEngine + B1, B2); the test asserts the header ids equal that list in order, each old title occurs exactly once, every class is ported/re-baselined/retired, 10 named stop-at-once and waiting-on-cancel tests are re-baselined, 25-27 retired, and each entry has exactly one new test titled with its id and class; ported titles equal the old titles. And (re-baselined names its decision): each re-baselined entry's leading parenthesis names D<n>, AD-<n>, owner ruling <n> or default <n>, each a known input; the reason also says what changed; the new test title carries the same names; 6, 9, 11, 12, 13, 21, 24 name D3 and 14 names default 4. I judged default 4 afresh: it is the spec's recorded prepare-goal decision (spec.md Prepare-goal defaults, derived from D3) and tasks.md T1.7 requires exactly that name, so it is the decision that changed test 14. And (retired names its replacing guard): each of 25-27 states why its input is gone and Replaced by a quoted guard, the new title carries it, and the test runs all three guards on the real engine (identical snapshot for a no-move fact and unknown ids T7.c1, T7, S99; a foreign snapshot dies). And (every listed test runs as a fact sequence through initial, apply and selectors): imports exclude the machine module and the port; fold helpers are pinned to engine.initial/engine.apply; each listed body is scanned for forbidden internals (TaskMachine, transition, createActor, casts, State params, context.units/moves/stop/warning, .value) and must fold and read through view/selectors; B1/B2 fold through TaskCommand.sliceOf, which uses TaskEvents.fold with this engine; a nested bun test runs the 29 listed tests and all 29 pass. Accepted readings: test 1 (is named xstate) reads only the engine's name member, as the old test did, so it has no facts to fold; some bodies read context.log (proved identical to view().history) and a phase tag via hasTag. Neither weakens the step's intent.
